sources.note: Nothing on Himarimã phonology. States the group lives in voluntary isolation, 'we do not know whether they are a single group speaking one language or several groups', and that one child contacted in 1986 'provided a list of 105 words of his language to Adolpho Killian' (fn 9: 'See Killian (n.d.)'). Its phonology chapter is about Suruwahá, a different language.
